signatures.name: MetalLB speaker errors
signatures.meaning: ARP/BGP announcement of the external IP failed, so it is unreachable from outside. `failed to announce service` (speaker), `failed to send ARP reply` (also used for NDP), `failed to send BGP update|withdraw|keepalive` are the named lines; the first alternative counts every other error-level line of the speaker and controller pods except `partial join`.
signatures.cause: Interface selection, L2Advertisement settings, node network.
signatures.verify: kubectl logs -n metallb-system -l component=speaker --since=1h | grep '"level":"error"' | grep -v 'partial join' | head

signatures.name: fluent-bit chunk flush failed
signatures.pattern: failed to flush chunk|could not flush|HTTP status=(4|5)\d\d
signatures.meaning: Logs are not being written to the output (Elasticsearch, Loki, CloudWatch) and are retrying. Past the retry limit they are dropped. The lines are "[ warn] [engine] failed to flush chunk '...', retry in N seconds" (one per retry) and the output plugin's "[error] ... HTTP status=NNN URI=..." or "could not flush records to host:port"; the HTTP response body follows on its own lines.
signatures.cause: Output target down or rejecting (ES disk watermark, mapping conflict), authentication, network.
signatures.verify: kubectl logs -n <ns> -l app.kubernetes.io/name=fluent-bit --since=1h | grep -c 'failed to flush'

signatures.name: fluent-bit cannot connect to its output
signatures.pattern: no upstream connections available|upstream connection initialization error|[Cc]onnection refused|[Cc]onnection timed out|connection #\d+ to \S+ timed out|broken connection
signatures.meaning: The connection to the output target itself fails. Logs pile up in the memory/file buffer and are eventually dropped. The lines are "[error] [output:...] no upstream connections available", "[error] [src/flb_...c:NNN errno=111] Connection refused" (glibc wording), "[upstream] connection #N to host:port timed out after N seconds" and "[http_client] broken connection to host:port ?".
signatures.cause: Elasticsearch or Loki down, changed Service name/port, network policy.

signatures.name: ACME challenge validation failed
signatures.pattern: propagation check failed|error (getting solver for|cleaning up|accepting) challenge|error waiting for authorization
signatures.meaning: Proof of domain ownership is not passing. Issuance is delayed. Up to 1.20.x the challenge controller logs `propagation check failed` on every self-check; from 1.21.0 the propagation wait is only a V(4) line and the Challenge status reason (`Waiting for HTTP-01 challenge propagation`, read by the verify command), so only the solver, cleanup, accept and authorization errors remain in the log.
signatures.cause: DNS record propagation delay, ingress not serving the .well-known path, firewall.

signatures.name: MetalLB speaker cannot reach a peer speaker
signatures.meaning: A speaker pod that the API server still lists is not reachable on port 7946, so the memberlist join to it times out. The speaker retries once a minute and logs this at level error each time; the speakers that are up keep announcing. It means a node is down (its speaker pod stays listed until evicted) or the memberlist port is blocked between nodes.
signatures.cause: Node NotReady or powered off, a firewall or NetworkPolicy blocking TCP/UDP 7946 between nodes.
signatures.verify: kubectl get nodes; kubectl get pods -n metallb-system -l component=speaker -o wide; kubectl logs -n metallb-system -l component=speaker --since=1h | grep -c 'partial join'

signatures.name: TLS Secret without an owning Certificate (not managed by cert-manager)
signatures.pattern: unable to fetch certificate that owns the secret.*not found
signatures.meaning: A TLS Secret carries cert-manager annotations but its Certificate resource is gone. An Ingress may be serving a certificate that will never renew (discovered at expiry). The cainjector prints the line on every event of such a Secret, so the count is events, not Secrets; the verify command lists the Secrets.
signatures.cause: Certificate deleted but Secret left behind, a namespace move, a hand-made Secret.
signatures.verify: kubectl get secrets -A --field-selector type=kubernetes.io/tls -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["cert-manager.io/certificate-name"]) | .metadata.namespace+"/"+.metadata.name' ; kubectl get certificates -A
